FRBRname.value: Loi du 30 avril 1997 sur les télécommunications (LTC)

preface.p: English is not an official language of the Swiss Confederation. This translation is provided for information purposes only and has no legal force.

preamble.p: The Federal Assembly of the Swiss Confederation,

based on Article 92 of the Constitution
SR 101 ,
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559). and having regard to the Federal Council Dispatch of 10 June 1996
BBl 1996 III 1405 ,

content.p: The aim of this Act is to ensure that a range of cost-effective, high quality, and nationally and internationally competitive telecommunications services is available to private individuals and the business community.

blockList.listIntroduction: It shall in particular:

item.p: ensure that a reliable universal service is provided, at affordable prices, for all sections of the population in all parts of the country;
ensure that telecommunications traffic is free from interference and respects personal and incorporeal property rights;
allow effective competition in the provision of telecommunications services;

item.num:
d.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951). Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 July 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).
item.p: protect users of telecommunications services from unfair advertising and from abuse associated with value-added services;

item.num:
e.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).
item.p: protect children and minors from the risks that arise from using telecommunications services.

authorialNote.p: Amended by Annex No II 2 of the FA of 24 March 2006 on Radio and Television, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 737; BBl 2003 1569).

content.p:
This Act shall regulate the transmission of information by means of telecommunications techniques, including the transmission of radio and television programme services, provided the Federal Act of 24 March 2006
SR 784.40 on Radio and Television (RTVA) does not prescribe otherwise.

blockList.listIntroduction: In this Act:

item.p: information means signs, signals, characters, images, sounds and any other form of representation addressed to human or other living beings or to machines;
telecommunications service means transmission of information for third parties by means of telecommunications techniques;

transmission by means of telecommunications techniques means sending or receiving of information, by lines or radio, by means of electrical, magnetic or optical signals or other electromagnetic signals;

item.num:
cbis.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).
item.p: public telephony service means a telecommunications service for the transmission of speech in real time by means of one or more addressing resources provided for this purpose in a national or international numbering plan;

item.num:
cter.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).
item.p: value-added service means a service provided by means of a telecommunications service and charged to the customers by their telecommunications service provider in addition to telecommunications services;
telecommunications installations means apparatus, lines or equipment intended for the transmission of information by means of telecommunications techniques or used for that purpose;

item.num:
dbis. and dter.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951). Repealed by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, with effect from 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

e.

item.p: interconnection means establishment of access by the connection of the installations and services of two telecommunications service providers, enabling them to operate together logically and in accordance with telecommunications techniques and allowing access to the services of third parties;

item.num:
ebis.
Inserted by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).
item.p: leased lines means provision of transparent transmission capacities via point-to-point connections;

eter.

item.p: cable ducts means underground pipes in which lines for transmission of information by telecommunications techniques are conveyed, including the access shafts;

item.num:
f.
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).
item.p: addressing resource means a sequence of digits, letters, signs or other information that enable the persons taking part in a telecommunications operation, as well as the computer processes, machines, apparatus or telecommunications installations involved, to be identified;

item.num:
g.
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).
item.p: directory data means information that identifies or designates a customer in relation to an individually assigned addressing element and which is used in order to publish a directory or is required for the provision of a telecommunications service;

item.num:
h.

item.p:
radio and television programme service means sequence of programmes as defined in Article 2 RTVA
SR 784.40 .

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council shall submit a report to the Federal Assembly every three years on:

item.p: the development of investments made throughout Switzerland;
the development of the universal provision of services;
the quality and the prices of the telecommunications services on offer;
the development of network competition;
the costs and granting of access to the local loop, irrespective of the technology underlying these connections.

content.p: If required, the Federal Council shall submit proposals to the Federal Assembly for promoting effective competition.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Office of Communications (OFCOM) shall register telecommunications service providers that use any of the following resources intended for providing telecommunications services:

item.p: radio frequencies whose use requires a licence;
addressing resources that are managed at national level.

content.p: Registered providers may allow other telecommunications service providers to use resources under paragraph 1 only if these other providers have registered beforehand.
OFCOM shall maintain and publish a list of registered providers and the telecommunications services that they offer.
The Federal Council shall regulate the details of registration.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

article.heading: Telecommunications service providers organised under foreign law

content.p: The competent authority may, subject to any international obligations to the contrary, prohibit telecommunications service providers organised under foreign law from using radio frequencies or addressing resources under Article 4 paragraph 1 unless reciprocal rights are granted.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

article.heading: Telecommunications service providers with registered office or permanent settlement in Switzerland

blockList.listIntroduction: Telecommunications service providers with a registered office or permanent settlement in Switzerland must:

item.p: comply with the employment regulations and guarantee the conditions of employment customary in the industry;
offer an appropriate number of vocational education and training places for apprentices.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Annex No II 3 of the FA of 18 March 2016 on the Surveillance of Postal and Telecommunications Traffic, in force since 1 March 2018 (AS 2018 117; BBl 2013 2683).

blockList.listIntroduction: Providers of telecommunications services must block the access to telephone and internet services for persons who have established a customer relationship that is not based on a subscription where these persons on establishing the customer relationship:

item.p: have used the identity of a person who does not exist or who has not previously consented to establishing the customer relationship; or

has failed to provide a document that meets the requirements imposed by the Federal Council under Article 23 paragraph 1 of the Federal Act of 18 March 2016
SR 780.1 on the Surveillance of Postal and Telecommunications Traffic.

article.num:
Art. 7–10
Repealed by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, with effect from 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).

authorialNote.p: Amended by Art. 106 para. 2 of the FA of 24 March 2006 on Radio and Television, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 737; BBl 2003 1569).

article.heading: Granting of access by dominant providers

blockList.listIntroduction:
Providers of telecommunications services that have a dominant position in the market must provide access to other providers in a transparent and non-discriminatory manner at cost-oriented prices in the following forms to their facilities and services:
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

item.num:
a.
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).
item.p: fully unbundled access to the local loop in order to use the entire frequency spectrum of the twisted pair metallic line;

item.num:
b. and c.
Repealed by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, with effect from 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

item.p: interconnection;
leased lines;
access to cable ducts, provided these have sufficient capacity.

content.p: They shall disclose the conditions and prices for their individual access services separately.
The Federal Council regulates the details.

Providers of telecommunications services shall provide OFCOM
Term in accordance with No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559). This change has been made throughout the text. with a copy of their access agreement. Unless there is some overriding public or private interest not to do so, OFCOM shall allow agreements to be consulted.
There is no obligation to guarantee access in relation to the broadcasting of radio and television programme services.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).

content.p:
If providers of telecommunications services do not agree within three months on the access conditions, the Federal Communications Commission (ComCom) shall decide at the request of one party and based on the proposal made by OFCOM.
Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559). It shall take particular account of the conditions which promote effective competition, as well as the effects of its decision on competing companies. It may accord interim legal protection.
If the question of dominance in the market must be assessed, OFCOM shall consult the Competition Commission. The latter may publish its position.

ComCom
Term in accordance with No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559). This change has been made throughout the text. shall decide within seven months of receipt of the request.
It shall regulate the type and form of accounting and financial information which dominant providers of telecommunications services must submit in the procedure in accordance with para. 1.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).

article.heading: Disputes arising from agreements and decisions regarding access

content.p: Disputes arising from agreements and decisions regarding access shall be judged by the civil courts.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).

content.p: Dominant providers of telecommunications services may bundle their services, provided they also offer the services included in the bundle individually.
Services need not be offered individually if they can only be offered in the bundle for technical, economic, quality or security reasons.
If a provider of telecommunications services bundles its own services with services of a third party undertaking which this provider controls or is controlled by, paragraphs 1 and 2 apply.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951). Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

article.heading: Obligations of transparency and to provide information

content.p: The telecommunications service providers must guarantee that their prices are transparent to their customers.
They shall inform the public concerning the quality of the telecommunications services that they provide.
The Federal Council shall specify the information that the providers must publish.
OFCOM may inform the public about the various telecommunications services offered by the providers.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Council may issue regulations on international roaming in order to avoid unreasonably high end customer tariffs, and may take measures to encourage competition. It may in particular:

item.p: issue regulations on billing procedures;
require mobile telephony providers to allow their customers to use the roaming services of third-party providers when abroad;
fix price limits based on international agreements;
require mobile telephony providers to offer bundled services including roaming services as well as options that allow the use of roaming services at fixed prices or reduced standard prices.

content.p: OFCOM shall conduct market monitoring procedures and analyse technical and price-related developments. In doing so, it shall rely in particular on the information obtained from providers under Article 59 paragraph 1 and shall work with the Price Supervisor.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951). Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

blockList.listIntroduction: To prevent abuses, the Federal Council shall regulate value-added services by taking the following measures in particular:

item.p: fixing price limits;
issuing regulations on the recognisability of value-added services;
fixing the amounts above which a charge may only be made with the express consent of the users;
subject to compliance with international obligations, requiring that providers of value-added services have their registered office or a permanent settlement in Switzerland.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

content.p: If a customer disputes an invoice from their telecommunications service provider for services other than telecommunications services, the provider is not permitted for this reason to block access to telecommunications services nor to terminate the contract before the dispute is settled.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).

content.p: OFCOM shall establish a dispute resolution service or shall entrust this to third parties. In the event of disputes between customers and providers of telecommunications services or value-added services, either party may invoke the service.

The party invoking the dispute resolution service shall pay a handling fee. The provider of telecommunications services or value-added services shall bear the costs of the procedure minus the handling fee.
The parties are not bound by the dispute resolution decision.
The Federal Council regulates the details.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951). Amended by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

content.p: Customers of telecommunications services shall have the option of having their details recorded in the public directories. They may within the limits set under paragraph 2 decide which directory data pertaining to them may be published.
The Federal Council may specify which data a directory entry must include as a minimum. It may regulate the details of publication and the use of the data.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

content.p: The providers of internet access shall transmit information without making any technical or commercial distinction between senders, recipients, content, services, service classes, protocols, applications, programmes or terminals.

blockList.listIntroduction: They may transmit information by different methods if this is required in order to:

item.p: comply with a statutory requirement or court decision;
guarantee the integrity or security of the network, the services provided on this network or the terminals connected to it;
comply with an express request from the customer; or
overcome temporary and exceptional network congestion; in doing so, equivalent forms of data traffic shall be treated equally.

content.p: In addition to internet access, they may offer other services via the same connection which must be optimised for specific content, applications or services in order to meet the quality requirements of customers. These other services must not be usable or offered as a substitute for internet access services, and they must not degrade the quality of internet access services.
If they handle information in a different technical or economic manner during transmission, they must inform their customers and the public of this.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).

content.p: Unless there is an overriding public or private interest in not doing so, OFCOM shall on request provide the name and address of the provider of telecommunications services or value-added services, and information on the services provided by it and any administrative or criminal prosecutions and penalties.
It may publish this information and make it accessible online if there is a public interest.
Only in the case of overriding public or private interest may it provide information on ongoing administrative or criminal prosecutions, publish that information or make it accessible online.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).

content.p:
The Commission and the Federal Office may process personal data, including data concerning administrative or criminal prosecutions and sanctions, provided that this is indispensable for the fulfilment of their tasks under the telecommunications legislation.
Amended by Annex 1 No II 68 of the Data Protection Act of 25 Sept. 2020, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 491; BBl 2017 6941). They may use an information system for this purpose.
They shall take the technical and organisational measures necessary for data protection and security during processing, and in particular during transmission.

The Federal Council may issue complementary provisions, namely concerning the organisation and operation of the information system, the categories of the data to be processed, access and processing authorisations, the term of conservation as well as the archiving and destruction of data.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).

content.p:
ComCom and OFCOM shall provide to other Swiss authorities data which these authorities need in order to fulfil their legal duties. This data also includes sensitive data obtained in administrative or administrative criminal proceedings.
Second sentence amended by Annex 1 No II 68 of the Data Protection Act of 25 Sept. 2020, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 491; BBl 2017 6941). The data shall be made accessible individually, in lists or on electronic media.

blockList.listIntroduction:
Subject to international agreements to the contrary, the Commission and the Federal Office may only transfer data to foreign surveillance authorities in the telecommunications sector, including sensitive personal data obtained in administrative or administrative criminal proceedings, if these authorities:
Amended by Annex 1 No II 68 of the Data Protection Act of 25 Sept. 2020, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 491; BBl 2017 6941).

item.p: use such data exclusively to conduct surveillance of telecommunications service providers or for purposes of market surveillance;
are bound by official or professional secrecy; and

forward this data to competent authorities and bodies which are entrusted with surveillance tasks in the public interest only with the prior consent of ComCom or OFCOM or on the basis of a general authorisation in a treaty.

content.p: ComCom and OFCOM shall not forward data to foreign prosecuting authorities if legal assistance is excluded in criminal matters. ComCom or OFCOM shall decide in agreement with the Federal Office of Justice.

Swiss authorities shall forward to the Commission and the Federal Office without charge such data as may be important for the enforcement of telecommunications legislation, including sensitive personal data.
Amended by Annex 1 No II 68 of the Data Protection Act of 25 Sept. 2020, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 491; BBl 2017 6941). The data shall be made accessible individually, in lists or on electronic media.

section.heading:
Universal Service Licence
Amended by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).

content.p: ComCom shall ensure that the universal service is guaranteed for all sections of the population in all parts of the country. To this end, it shall periodically grant one or more universal service licences.
The licence shall be tied to the condition that all or specific services of the universal service (Art. 16) are provided to all sectors of the population within the area covered by the licence.

An invitation to tender shall be issued for the granting of the licence. The procedure shall be conducted in accordance with the principles of objectivity, non-discrimination and transparency. The Federal Council regulates the details. The law on public procurement does not apply.
Fourth sentence inserted by No I of the FA of 22 March 2019, in force since 1 Jan. 2021 (AS 2020 6159; BBl 2017 6559).

If it is clear in advance that the invitation to tender cannot proceed under conditions of competition, or if it does not produce any suitable candidates, ComCom may appoint one or more providers of telecommunications services to guarantee the universal service.
Licences are generally limited to the same term.

blockList.listIntroduction: Any person wishing to obtain a universal service licence must:

item.p: have the necessary technical capacities;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).
item.p: furnish convincing proof that the service can be offered, particularly with regard to finance, and the service operated for the entire duration of the licence, and state what financial compensation, in accordance with Article 19, will be required;
undertake to comply with the applicable legislation, in particular this Act and its implementing provisions, and the licence conditions;

item.num:
d.
Amended by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).
item.p: undertake to comply with employment legislation and to guarantee the working conditions that are customary in the sector.

article.heading:
Scope of the universal service
Amended by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).

blockList.listIntroduction:
The universal service licensee shall provide one or more of the following services to meet demand in the area covered by the licence, in accordance with the state of the art:
Amended by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).

item.num:
a.
Amended by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).
item.p: a public telephone service, i.e. transmission of speech in real time by means of telecommunications techniques, including transmission of data employing transfer rates compatible with the channels for transmitting speech, as well as the connection and additional services;
access to emergency call services;
public pay telephones in sufficient numbers;

item.num:
d.
Amended by No I of the FA of 24 March 2006, in force since 1 Apr. 2007 (AS 2007 921; BBl 2003 7951).
item.p: access to the Swiss directories of subscribers to the public telephone service; the Federal Council may require a universal service licensee to maintain a directory of all customers of services of the universal service (general directory);

item.num:
e.
